subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Time, Temperature, and Turbulence
description: A fast breakdown of Time, Temperature, and Turbulence for builders.

hook.text: Three variables control extraction: how long, how hot, and how much agitation the water gets.

buildup.text: Longer brew time extracts more. An espresso runs 25 seconds; cold brew steeps 12–24 hours.

discovery.text: Hotter water extracts faster. The ideal range is 90–96°C. Boiling water scorches and over-extracts.

twist.text: Cold brew breaks the rules—low temperature plus extreme time produces a smooth, low-acid concentrate.

climax.text: Stirring or pouring (turbulence) speeds extraction. A French press gets agitated; drip coffee doesn't.

punchline.text: Three dials, infinite results. Brewing is applied physics.

quiz.question: What is the ideal water temperature for brewing coffee?
